test_title: PYST 40: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following missions marked the 100th launch of ISRO from India’s Spaceport Sriharikota, boosting India’s standing in space launch capability?

options.text: Launch of NVS‑02 navigation satellite on GSLV-F15

solution:
The correct answer is __**Launch of NVS-02 navigation satellite on GSLV-F15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Launch of NVS-02 navigation satellite on GSLV-F15** is recognized in this context as the milestone marking the **100th launch** from **India’s Spaceport** located at **Sriharikota**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• This mission utilized the **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F15)**, which is a three-stage launch vehicle designed to place satellites into **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
• The **NVS-02** is a part of the second-generation satellite series for the **Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC)**, aimed at providing accurate and real-time positioning and timing services over **India** and the surrounding region.
 
• The **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) SHAR** in **Sriharikota** has been the primary orbital launch site for **ISRO** since its first launch in **1979** (the **SLV-3**).
 
• Reaching the **100th launch** milestone at a single spaceport signifies **India's** growing self-reliance and commercial viability in the global space market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Launch of Aditya-L1 solar observatory:**
 
 
• This was **India's** first dedicated solar mission, launched on **September 2, 2023**.
 
• It was launched using the **PSLV-C57** rocket and placed at the **Lagrangian Point 1 (L1)** to study the **Sun's** corona and solar winds. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Launch of INSAT-3DS weather satellite:**
 
 
• Launched on **February 17, 2024**, via the **GSLV-F14** mission.
 
• It is an advanced meteorological satellite designed for enhanced monitoring of **Earth's** surface, oceanic observations, and weather forecasting. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Launch of Chandrayaan-3:**
 
 
• Launched on **July 14, 2023**, using the **LVM3-M4** (Launch Vehicle Mark-III) rocket.
 
• This mission successfully performed a soft landing on the **Lunar South Pole** on **August 23, 2023**, making **India** the first country to do so. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) SHAR:**
 
 
• Located in **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**, it features two active launch pads.
 
• It was named after **Prof. Satish Dhawan**, the former Chairman of **ISRO**, in **2002**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation):** Formerly known as **IRNSS**, it consists of a constellation of **7 to 9 satellites** providing **Standard Positioning Service (SPS)** for civilians and **Restricted Service (RS)** for strategic users.
 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation):** Formed on **August 15, 1969**, with its headquarters in **Bengaluru**. It operates under the **Department of Space**.
 
• **Launch Vehicles:** **ISRO** utilizes various vehicles including **PSLV** (the "workhorse"), **GSLV** (for heavier payloads), **LVM3** (the heaviest launcher), and the **SSLV** (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle).
 
• The **NVS** series satellites incorporate **L1, L5, and S-band** signals and, for the first time, carry an indigenous **Rubidium atomic clock** for high-precision timing.
